prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2015 — summary (under 500 words)

- Fiscal rules and tax
  - Budget Responsibility Lock: no new borrowing to fund pledges; OBR audit of manifestos; cut the deficit every year; get debt falling and a current-budget surplus ASAP.
  - Fairer taxes: restore 50p top rate; introduce a 10p starting rate (paid for by ending Marriage Allowance); no rises in basic/higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; abolish non‑dom status; tougher anti‑avoidance and HMRC reform.

- Economy, business and infrastructure
  - British Investment Bank and regional banks; most competitive G7 corporation tax; cut/freeze small business rates; tackle late payment.
  - Corporate governance reforms: long‑termism, employee voice on pay, investor voting transparency.
  - National Infrastructure Commission; HS2 with cost control; better northern rail; roads, cycling; universal affordable high‑speed broadband and wider mobile coverage.
  - Green industrial strategy: decarbonise electricity by 2030; 1m additional green jobs; empower Green Investment Bank; balanced energy mix.

- Work, skills and young people
  - Minimum Wage >£8/hour by Oct 2019; promote Living Wage via procurement and first‑year tax rebates; reporting by listed firms.
  - Ban exploitative zero‑hours (12‑week regular-hours right to a contract); close agency-worker loopholes; scrap employment tribunal fees.
  - Apprenticeship guarantee for qualified school‑leavers; more public‑sector apprenticeships; technical degrees; curb unpaid internships.
  - Cut university fees to £6,000; Youth and long‑term unemployed Compulsory Jobs Guarantee (funded by bank bonus tax).

- Families and housing
  - Free childcare 25 hours for working parents of 3–4s; wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave to 4 weeks and increase pay.
  - Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; “use it or lose it” land powers; support small builders; new garden cities; Future Homes Fund.
  - Private renting: three‑year tenancies as standard with limits on rent rises; ban letting fees; landlord register.
  - Abolish the Bedroom Tax.

- NHS and social care
  - 20,000 nurses, 8,000 GPs, 3,000 midwives (funded by Mansion Tax, tobacco levy, anti‑avoidance).
  - 48‑hour GP appointments; one‑week cancer tests by 2020; Cancer Treatments Fund.
  - Repeal marketisation rules; cap private profits; protect NHS from TTIP; integrate physical, mental and social care with personal plans and single coordinator.
  - Mental health parity, faster access to talking therapies; end 15‑minute care visits; 5,000 home‑care workers; better support for carers.

- Education
  - Protect full education budget (early years to post‑16); all teachers qualified; cap infant classes at 30.
  - Directors of School Standards; end Free Schools programme.
  - Technical Baccalaureate; Institutes of Technical Education; compulsory SRE; tackle bullying; continued English/Maths to 18; improved careers advice.

- Consumer markets and bills
  - Freeze energy prices to 2017 and reform market (separate generation/supply, tougher watchdog); mass home energy‑efficiency.
  - Stronger water and rail regulation; allow a public rail operator; freeze rail fares next year and cap rises; devolved bus powers and smart ticketing.

- Immigration, policing and security
  - Full exit checks; 1,000 extra border staff; two‑year wait for EU migrants’ benefits; English requirement for public‑facing staff; stop wage undercutting and rogue agencies.
  - Protect neighbourhood policing (scrap PCCs) and safeguard 10,000 officers; new Police Standards Authority; victims’ law; Violence Against Women and Girls Bill and commissioner; tougher extremism measures with stronger oversight.

- Devolution and democracy
  - English Devolution Act: £30bn and powers to regions; Constitutional Convention; replace House of Lords with elected Senate; votes at 16.
  - Tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships; more powers for Scotland and Wales; fair funding floor for Wales.

- Rights, media, environment, and world
  - Keep Human Rights Act; extend FOI; gender pay‑gap reporting; race equality strategy; strengthen LGBT rights; media plurality and Leveson.
  - Lead on climate action (Paris deal; net‑zero in second half of century); flood prevention and clean air.
  - Defence review; maintain NATO commitment and nuclear deterrent; bolster cyber security.
  - Stay in and reform the EU; referendum lock on any future power transfer.
  - Keep 0.7% aid; focus on poorest; Centre for Universal Health Coverage.
